blocks.content: The Constitution visualises the UPSC to be the 'watch-dog of merit system' in India.

rows: Recruitment and merit-based selection of civil servants
Consulted on disciplinary actions against civil servants
Investigates vigilance-related misconduct and corruption cases

items: UPSC is NOT consulted on matters regarding reservation of appointments or posts in favour of any backward class of citizens.
The Parliament, not the executive, has the authority to extend the jurisdiction and additional functions of the UPSC.
Recommendations made by the UPSC are advisory in nature and not binding on the executive government.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: UPSC conducts examinations for appointments to All-India Services, Central Services, and Public Services of Union Territories.
Assists states in framing and operating schemes of joint recruitment whenever requested by two or more states.
Mandatory consultation on all disciplinary matters affecting civil servants serving the Government of India.
Submits an annual performance report to the President, which is laid before both Houses of Parliament along with a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice.
Functions as the central recruiting agency in India, whereas the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) acts as the central personnel agency.
